rendered:
The document doesn't give a sensitivity or detection limit for S. typhimurium in human serum.[1] The serum work tested whether the array could tell bacteria apart, not how little of each it could detect. In spiked human serum, the paper says that the clusters of all seven bacteria were well classified with almost no overlapping[2] (Fig. 5[3]). S. typhimurium is among those bacteria, and its cluster is labelled in the serum LDA plot.[4]

The only detection limits in the paper come from tests run outside serum, and they cover other species. P. aeruginosa: OD600 =0.0034[5] by CD. L. monocytogenes: 0.0123[6] by CD. When concentration was varied, S. typhimurium was among the strains for which only partial discrimination[7] was achieved.
